page: Amazon Web Services r7g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this server features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz with a dedicated CPU allocation and no hyperthreading. The processor is based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 model, equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks AVX and AMX instruction sets but includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance is provisioned with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and relies on the Nitro hypervisor. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7g.16xlarge demonstrates strong memory performance, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong read-only memory bandwidth of 253.34 GB/sec for large blocks. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 97897.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20513.0. Software compilation with Clang is top-tier, reaching 59595.0. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a strong PassMark database score and 101.19 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-core performance remains average across stress-ng and Geekbench tests. LLM text generation performance is mixed, showing weak throughput for small 135M models but strong throughput for medium 7B models.

The arm64 architecture of the Graviton processor provides high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Because the instance lacks local SSD storage, workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space must rely on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The r7g.16xlarge is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale Redis caches, relational databases, software compilation pipelines, and medium-sized language model inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 64-core AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors on an arm64 architecture. Operating at 2.6 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation and no hyperthreading, it features 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data reveals top-tier memory performance and software compilation speeds, alongside strong multi-core CPU capabilities and database operations, including 101.19 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation remain average to weak. This profile makes the r7g.16xlarge highly efficient for memory-heavy workloads, such as large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and concurrent software compilation, where high memory bandwidth and core density are critical.
